starting.label: ledger/api/routes.py
starting.reason: As intended: `api/routes` wires in `alerts` and the cache and drops the export; it stays the one box that assembles services and stores.

starting.label: ledger/services/alerts.py → ledger/storage
starting.reason: Skips the store layer: `services/alerts` reads `storage/db` directly, while `billing` reaches it only through `invoices` and `customers`. The title asks for alerts, not for a second way into `db`, which now has callers in two layers.

starting.label: ledger/services/billing.py → ledger/storage
starting.reason: Tied to the wrapper: expected that `billing` reads through the cache, but it now imports `cache` by name, so the service depends on two levels of `storage/` at once.

starting.label: ledger/services/legacy_export.py
starting.reason: Orphan removed: not in the title, but `legacy_export` and its endpoint had no caller in `web/src/`. Removing them takes a box, two endpoints and an edge into `storage/invoices` out of the graph, and `api/routes` loses a dependency.

starting.label: ledger/storage/cache.py
starting.reason: A layer inside storage/: the cache is what the title promises, but `cache` sits beside the store it wraps and depends on `invoices`, so `storage/` now has a level of its own. Should it live between `services/` and `storage/` instead?

starting.label: ledger/storage/db.py → ledger/services/alerts.py
starting.reason: New cycle: `storage/db` now imports `services/alerts`, which imports `storage/db`. The lowest box of the backend depends on a service, so every store sits in the cycle too; nothing in the title asks the database to know about alerts.

starting.label: web/src/client.ts → GET alerts/overdue
starting.reason: Client becomes a hub: expected from the title, but `client` now serves both `/customers` and `/alerts`, and every view goes through it. Split it per area as more arrive?

starting.label: web/src/views/alerts.ts
starting.reason: Follows the pattern: the new `views/alerts` reaches the backend only through `client`, like `views/account`; no view calls an endpoint of its own.
